conversation.content:
Hello! I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply 10 questions about your mood, thoughts, and energy in the past week. Your answers stay private and help us see what extra support—if any—might help you feel more like yourself again. We’ll go one question at a time, and you can answer however feels comfortable. Ready to begin?

Question 1/10  
Over the past seven days, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, Doctor, I’ve had a few moments where something makes me smile, but I don’t feel that easy, light laughter I used to. It’s like the joy gets stuck before it comes out. Maybe once or twice the whole week I actually laughed, and even then it felt kind of forced.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Most days I haven’t, really… maybe one or two times I sort of chuckled, but it didn’t feel natural. I have to think hard to remember the last time I actually laughed out loud.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much, Doctor. I used to get excited about little plans—grabbing coffee with a friend, even just a quiet shower—but lately it feels like I’m just getting through the day. I still try to set up small things for myself, yet when the time comes I’m kind of “meh,” like the spark isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times this week. When the baby wouldn’t settle or I couldn’t get the swaddle right, I kept thinking, “Other moms manage—why can’t I figure it out?” I know, rationally, babies just cry, but in the moment I still hear that little voice saying I must be doing something wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I’d say yes, several days this week. Like, I’ll be sitting there feeding her and suddenly my chest feels tight because I’m sure she’s breathing funny—even though she’s perfectly fine. Or I’ll worry the bottle temp is off, or that I missed a spot sanitizing the pump parts. Nothing huge triggered it; the thoughts just pop in and I can’t shake them for a while.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Maybe once or twice. It’s not like a full panic attack, but I’ll suddenly get this rush—heart racing, can’t catch my breath—because I imagine something awful happening to her, like SIDS or choking, even though she’s right there and fine. The feeling passes after a few minutes, but yeah, it’s kind of scary when it hits out of nowhere.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days. It’s not one big thing—just the constant cycle of feeding, changing, trying to sleep, then starting over. Some mornings I open my eyes and already feel behind. I manage, but it’s like I’m wading through thick water; everything feels heavier and harder than it should.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s happened a few nights. I’ll finally get her down, but then my mind keeps circling—did I burp her long enough, did I fasten the diaper snug, is she still breathing—so I lie there wide-eyed. Even when I’m exhausted, it can take an hour or more to drift off, and then I jerk awake at every tiny grunt she makes.
I have felt sad or miserable

I’ve had days like that—maybe three or four this week. It’s not weeping-in-the-corner sad, just this dull, heavy feeling that sits on my chest. I’ll watch her sleep and instead of melting over her little yawns I feel kind of empty, like I’m missing the joy everyone says I should be flooded with. The sadness comes and goes, but when it’s here it just drains the color out of everything.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really… I got a little teary-eyed one evening when she wouldn’t latch and I felt useless, but actual crying—like full-on tears—maybe once the whole week. Mostly the sadness just sits there without spilling over.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, Doctor—never. I might feel overwhelmed or down, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. My baby needs me, and I want to be here for her.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 18: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh Plus Anxiety items – mother of 2-week-old infant

Symptoms endorsed (frequency ≥ 4 days/week unless noted):
- Marked anhedonia (loss of laughter, anticipatory enjoyment)  
- Persistent low mood / “empty” feeling (3-4 days)  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt over routine infant-care tasks  
- Unwarranted worries about infant safety; somatic anxiety (chest tightness)  
- Discrete panic-like surges (1-2 episodes)  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia linked to rumination  
- Sense of being overwhelmed by daily demands

Not present:
- Crying spells >1 episode/week  
- Self-harm ideation (explicitly denied)

Pattern: Symptoms present most days for at least one week, causing subjective distress but no functional incapacity or safety concern.

Screening significance: High endorsement of core depressive and anxiety items; meets threshold for further evaluation of postpartum depression and comorbid anxiety. No self-harm risk identified today.

Recommendation: Refer for comprehensive perinatal mental health assessment; consider standardized EPDS and GAD-7; monitor safety at each contact.
